comments.text: Two inverse screen-code digits copied into the status display; Mystery Maze file variants share number25.
Initial placement-stream pointer consumed by resident $7514/$4D0F before the private initialization callback.
Background and border color bytes. Loader uses pristine backup $3804/$3805 when publishing VIC colors.
Seven-byte bomb record pointer. The scanner searches for key $FF; target count $3013 need not equal record count. PLF13 uniquely omits the terminator after its four intended records.
Four pending callback pointers copied by $758A into $40C8-$40CF. A zero high byte leaves the existing no-op task; nonzero vectors are committed by the resident IRQ.
Initial player X low, X high and Y in hardware sprite coordinates, read by spawn $56E0. This is the start of each life, not multicolor drawing coordinates.
Initial target counter 14. Collection decrements it; special bomb callbacks can compensate the decrement or replace the table. Primary record list has 14 entries.
Resident perimeter-bullet slot limit 3; $6800 considers sprite slots1 through limit-minus-one. Private level actors can use other slots.
Ordinary collection adds this little-endian binary value (100) to the24-bit total score. Private callbacks may add an extra award first.
Initial little-endian bonus 1500. The resident countdown subtracts100 per256 enabled IRQ services; completion adds the remaining amount to total and bonus records.
Private initialization routine called after initial scenery drawing. Common no-op target is the RTS at $301F.
Main-thread entry selected by JMP($301B) at $759C; typically the spawn/collection/exit loop at $3050.
Private cleanup hook copied into the local JSR trampoline before completion or exhaustion. A target of $301F returns immediately.
Shared one-byte RTS used by empty initialization, cleanup and individual bomb callbacks in this overlay.
Eight ladder/up-rope X columns followed by six down-rope X columns, copied to $40B0-$40BD. Coordinates use160-wide multicolor space; $FF marks unavailable columns.
Two zero header bytes between the climb-column arrays and completion vector; the shared loader does not read them as part of those arrays.
Ordinary successful-level destination $5B00. The private loop calls cleanup before jumping through this word.
Exhausted-lives destination $5FFD, the resident jump to game-over presentation $6A80. This is separate from successful completion.
Two filename suffix characters '23'. Resident loader copies them into $40D3/$40D4; private cleanup can replace them before the next disk request.
Single $FF drawing-stream terminator, used as the no-change post-bomb action.
Zero byte after the empty drawing terminator and before collection-key coordinate offsets.
X/Y offsets applied by resident $55BF when reducing player position to the bomb lookup key. They adjust the coarse cell test, not the visible bomb positions.
Optional hook called before the matched bomb-record callback. A zero high byte suppresses the call; otherwise the resident patches JSR $5643 from this word.
Twenty loaded zero bytes align the private main loop to $3050. Header fields end at $303B; no private structure is assigned to this gap.

Spawn a life through $436A, poll status/input through $436D, and test bombs remaining at $3013. Zero bombs calls cleanup and jumps through completion vector $3030. Death mode 2 waits to become 0; reserves $40E4=$FF calls cleanup and jumps through exhaustion vector $3032, otherwise respawn. Cleanup vector $301D is invoked through a patched JSR.
Ignore player collision masks containing any sprite 5-7 bit, making freezing creatures nonlethal. Otherwise only hazard bits 1-2 ($06) start death, and only while player-active with mode 0.

Drawing data $30AD-$3131 read by Initial scenery $30AD. Stream commands are FE shape pointer, FD repeat delta, FC stream jump, x/y/count placement and FF end. Referenced shapes hold width/x-offset/y-offset/pixel rows endingFF; source pixel codes are0 background,1 bomb,2 support,3 climbable. Parsed by the same behavioral renderer checked against original $4D0F.

14 seven-byte records [coarse key,x,y,callback low/high,post-draw low/high]. Terminator: $FF. Coordinates are160-wide bitmap positions. The resident scanner matches the key, calls both hooks, adds $3015 points, erases the bomb, follows the draw pointer and decrements $3013. This list is not bounded by the target counter.

Drawing data $3195-$31CC read by Post-bomb drawing $3195, Post-bomb drawing $319F, Post-bomb drawing $31A9, Post-bomb drawing $31B6, Post-bomb drawing $31C0. Stream commands are FE shape pointer, FD repeat delta, FC stream jump, x/y/count placement and FF end. Referenced shapes hold width/x-offset/y-offset/pixel rows endingFF; source pixel codes are0 background,1 bomb,2 support,3 climbable. Parsed by the same behavioral renderer checked against original $4D0F.
Four packed 30-byte animated creature frames. The $4376 copier expands these to VIC frames $10-$13; the following 120 copied bytes populate frames that this animation never selects.
Call $4376 with X=$31, Y=$CD to expand the four creature frames at $31CD. Other creature state starts from the zero defaults loaded with the overlay.
Eight-byte workspace indexed by hardware sprite number; active slots 5-7 hold state: 0 unspawned, 1 tracking, 2 erratic after player contact.
Eight-byte workspace indexed by hardware sprite number; active slots 5-7 hold signed X velocity low byte.
Eight-byte workspace indexed by hardware sprite number; active slots 5-7 hold signed X velocity high byte.
Eight-byte workspace indexed by hardware sprite number; active slots 5-7 hold signed Y velocity.

Eight candidate motion directions, X low component. First four are cardinal; last four alternate diagonal X=+/-6 with Y=-3. Tracking selects cardinal directions; erratic movement can select all eight.

Eight candidate motion directions, X high component. First four are cardinal; last four alternate diagonal X=+/-6 with Y=-3. Tracking selects cardinal directions; erratic movement can select all eight.
Eight candidate motion directions, Y component. First four are cardinal; last four alternate diagonal X=+/-6 with Y=-3. Tracking selects cardinal directions; erratic movement can select all eight.
Modulo-3 movement divider, animation tick, and saved sprite index. Only every third eligible movement callback advances creatures.
After updating the creatures, tail-call $3439 to schedule the sound associated with sprite 7 frame $13.

Creature motion every third eligible callback, speed<9 and life!=2, independent of hazard pulse. Tracking uses quantized creature coordinates against unrounded player coordinates. Erratic state samples eight velocity entries with both upward diagonals duplicated: six distinct velocities, no downward diagonals. CPU checked cadence, boundaries and all eight original-RNG choices. Cache player half-X at$33C2 and set creature colours from$4047. Spawn atX6 with randomY<218/cardinal velocity; animate$10-$13 and use$33C3/$33CE for horizontal wrap.
Cached nine-bit player X divided by two, used by creature steering comparisons.
Horizontal edge handlers: crossing the low edge sets X-low=$5C and increments X-high; crossing the high edge resets X to 6. Rejoin the Y update. The final RTS is also shared by contact scanning.

After countdown, accepted creature shadow has playerbit0 and no$0E, with life0/speed<9. Reload timer80 and mark creature erratic. No player/hazard pulse gate. Live contact refreshes80 on frames1-3 and25-42; CPU exhausts masks and gate cases.

Before contact callback, nonzero timer forces direction$88/fire$11 and decrements. Entry1 becomes0 with overrides retained; following zero entry masks to$08/$10, then next input poll samples controls. Native input/control replay confirms phases and bullet death while frozen. Existing jump/fall physics can continue; only new input is suppressed.

Freeze countdown initialized/reloaded to80 by contact. Zero-entry clearing is a separate later callback. Suppresses new movement/jump input; an existing jump or fall can continue. It grants no general bullet immunity.
When sprite 7 frame pointer $4082 equals $13, queue effect $3455 with priority 3, release 0, control $40 (pulse). Other animation frames return without scheduling.
SID stream: envelope $11/$32, pulse width $8888, frequencies $1010, $0808, $0404 for two sound updates each, then zero terminator.
